newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Alumax sees consolidation. [CORRECTED 02:43 GMT 6/11]
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Alumax sees consolidation. [CORRECTED 02:43 GMT 6/11]

text.p: There may be further consolidation in the aluminium industry, said Alumax Inc Chief Executive Allen Born, although he saw no signs that his company was about to be the target of a takeover bid.
(Corrects, removing reference in headline to Alumax being a possible takeover target.)
"We are probably the most diversified and attractive kid on the block," Born told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday. "That doesn't mean anything, but the speculation is there all the time."
In February, Alumax, a leading U.S. aluminium producer, rebuffed an approach by Kaiser Aluminum Corp about a possible takeover.

Last month Brandywine Asset Management Chief Tony Hitschler said in Business Week that Alumax's shares were undervalued and that he thought a large foreign metals company could soon make an attractive offer for it.
Born said Brandywine had a sizable investment in Alumax.

He added that consolidation remained a possibility throughout much of the aluminium industry, although a combination of very large producers like Aluminum Co of America was improbable and the primary aluminium sector was more likely to see consolidation in Europe than in the United States.

Referring to acquisition talks announced last month between Alumax and Eduard Hueck GmBH and Co, a privately held German manufacturer of aluminium architectural products, he said Alumax is also constantly on the look-out for potential acquisitions.
"We've got four of five things under consideration all the time," he said.
In January Alumax completed the purchase of Cressona Aluminum Co, a manufacturer of extruded aluminium products, in a bid to improve its position in the fast-growing transportation market.

Alumax Executive Vice President George Stoe said the Cressona acquisition boosted the share of Alumax's revenues from the transportation sector to 23 percent from 15 percent last year, while the goal was to reach 30 to 35 percent by the year 2000.

He also said Alumax had won a contract to supply General Motors Corp with more than 200 million pounds of extruded aluminium products over 10 years for a pick-up truck model, while a 10-year contract for 40 million pounds of aluminium sheet had not been awarded yet.
